card.keepWhy: Done a thousand times, it found its way without light.
sources: Mahabharata, Adi Parva (the first book), the princes’ training under Drona: the wind puts out the lamp as Arjuna eats; he sees his hand finds his mouth by habit and begins practicing archery at night; Drona hears his bowstring, embraces him and promises to make him the greatest archer
Gudakesha, a name for Arjuna in the Bhagavad Gita (1.24, 2.9); Krishna addresses him so in 10.20 and 11.7
check: Chapter of the lamp story in the Adi Parva (around chapter 123 in the Critical Edition; section 132 in Ganguli); confirm.
Gudakesha: “the one who conquered sleep” is the popular reading; some read it as “thick-haired.” The lesson says “often explained as.” Confirm.

hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? is there something hard for you now that you wish came naturally? speaking up, a sport, a language.
options: then this story is for you. listen.
then pick one while you listen.
good. keep this one for when you do.

steps.line: One night, young Arjuna was eating dinner when the wind blew out the lamp.

steps.q: The lamp goes out in the middle of dinner. What do you guess Arjuna does?
o: Calls for someone to relight it
Keeps on eating, without a light
Leaves the rest for the morning
steps.why: He keeps eating. Then he stops, and thinks. Watch.

steps.line: He kept eating in the dark. Then he stopped.
My hand finds my mouth without any light, he thought. Because I’ve done it a thousand times.

steps.q: The Mahabharata adds a twist: Drona had secretly given the cook an order about Arjuna’s meals. What was it?
o: Always serve him an extra portion
Serve him last, after the others
Never serve him food in the dark
steps.why: “Never give Arjuna food in the dark.” The text doesn’t say why, and readers still wonder. Then the wind blew the lamp out anyway.

steps.q: His hand found his mouth with no light at all. What does Arjuna do with that thought?
o: Asks Drona to teach him by moonlight
Starts shooting arrows in the dark
Sits in the dark nightly to train his ears
steps.why: He went out that same night with his bow. Not a better lamp, a new habit.

steps.line: So that night, he went out and practiced archery in the dark. And the next night. And the next.

steps.q: Night after night, Arjuna trains alone in the dark. How does Drona find out?
o: He hears the bowstring twang at night
The cook tells him about the lamp
He sees arrows in the targets at dawn
steps.why: The Mahabharata says Drona heard the twang in the dark, came out, embraced him, and promised that no archer in the world would equal him.

steps.line: His teacher, Drona, found out and was amazed. Arjuna would become the greatest archer of his age.

steps.q: Later, Drona tested his students: aim at a wooden bird in a tree. He asked each one, “What do you see?” What did Arjuna say?
o: The whole bird, sitting on its branch
The tree, the bird, and you, my teacher
steps.why: His brothers saw the tree, the teacher, each other. Arjuna saw only the head (retellings often say the eye), and he alone was allowed to shoot.

steps.line: What’s hard now becomes natural with practice. Do it once more than you planned.
steps.label: today

say: here’s what i love. arjuna wasn’t born able to shoot in the dark. he noticed something small at dinner, and practiced.
drona’s greatest student became great by repetition. hindus honor that kind of practice, done with your whole heart, until a skill becomes part of you.

steps.q: Later, in the Gita, Krishna sometimes calls Arjuna Gudakesha, often explained as “the one who conquered sleep.” After this story, why might that name fit?
o: He kept watch over his brothers’ camp
He trained through the nights while others slept
He could see in the dark from birth
steps.why: Night after night, he chose the bow over sleep. Some read Gudakesha as “thick-haired” instead, but “master of sleep” is how many teachers explain it.

today.say: pick the thing you’re practicing, and do it once more today than you planned. many hindus offer their practice to god before they begin, with a short prayer or a bow. you can offer it, or just practice. it’s your choice.
options: then do it, even in the dark.
then pick one small thing. night one starts tonight.
